newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher, led by bank shares.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher, led by bank shares.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Sunday on very high volume as traders focused on bank shares, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.23 percent, or 3.38 points, to 277.77 on heavy all-share turnover of 195 million shekels against 207 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.16 percent higher at 286.06.

"The top Maof stocks led the market today, and most activity was concentrated in bank shares," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank. "The market continues to show strength. I don't think that we will see a consolidation in the near future."

Bank Leumi, the most active share, rose 2.0 percent to 537 agorot on turnover of 32.1 million shekels. The bank reported on Sunday first-quarter earnings per share of 44 agorot against eight agorot the same time last year. Leumi also completed a successful public offering last week.
Bank Hapoalim, the third most active issue, gained 2.75 percent to 789 agorot on volume of 27.4 million shekels.

"Despite expectations for a mild correction the market continues to rise. The market looks very good and from a technical point of view it is expected to continue rising in the near term," said Arik Rotstein of Bloch Rotstein Securities and Investments. "I believe that the Maof will reach 300 in two or three weeks."
Rotstein added that the increased trading activity also reflected the positive trend.
The Mizrahi trader agreed that the market is bullish. "Traders are very optimistic, but the positive trend is expected to continue on a slower pace," she said.
Osem Investments, lost 0.25 percent to 1,974 agorot after the company reported that earnings per share fell in the first quarter to 22 agorot from 25 agorot a year earlier.
Israel Corp fell 2.5 percent to 21,399 agorot. The company on Sunday reported a loss per share of 6.41 shekels against earnings per share of 7.21 shekels in the first quarter of 1996.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the second most active share, rose 2.75 percent to 20,506 agorot on volume of 6.7 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
